headline: High risk of prompt injection and data leakage: gpt-engineer writes project files while Perplexity ingests uploaded content and browses externally, creating a dangerous handoff path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-engineer writes files in a shared project directory and has no self-isolation by default; Perplexity can ingest uploaded documents and browsing context. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if gpt-engineer output is copied into Perplexity or vice versa. The pathway is not fully automatic, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF gpt-engineer output is pasted into Perplexity prompts or uploads
IF Perplexity-generated text is copied back into gpt-engineer task files
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Do not paste raw model output between agents
Add a human review step before reusing generated text
Use a fixed template for prompts and outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-engineer can read and write the project directory and may handle OPENAI_API_KEY, while Perplexity processes uploaded documents and browsing context through vendor-hosted APIs. If sensitive files are placed in the shared project directory and then uploaded or summarized by Perplexity, data can leave the local boundary. The profiles show a real shared-data path, but not an automatic leak.
conditions: IF sensitive files are stored in the project directory
IF those files are uploaded to Perplexity for analysis
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the project directory
Use a redacted copy before uploading documents
Restrict Perplexity to non-sensitive queries
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on uploads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-engineer has filesystem write and shell execution, while Perplexity has no host write or shell capability. Their write surfaces do not overlap directly, so there is little chance of simultaneous mutation conflict. The only shared state is indirect through user-managed project artifacts, which makes conflict possible but limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same project artifacts
IF the user manually merges edits from both agents
mitigations: Assign one agent as the sole writer
Use separate branches or copies
Merge changes manually after each turn
Lock the project directory during one agent's run

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer produces code and file edits that Perplexity can then summarize or cite, so Perplexity may treat upstream output as authoritative without verification. Perplexity's browsing/citation workflow can amplify mistakes from gpt-engineer into polished but incorrect answers or recommendations. This is a default interaction risk, though not clearly an autonomous action chain.
conditions: IF Perplexity is asked to explain or validate gpt-engineer-generated artifacts
IF downstream decisions rely on Perplexity summaries without independent checks
mitigations: Require source verification before acting on summaries
Ask Perplexity to quote primary sources only
Compare outputs against the original files
Flag generated code as untrusted until reviewed
requires-engineering: add automated validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and processes uploaded documents and browsing context, while gpt-engineer is local/project-directory based and may handle secrets like OPENAI_API_KEY. The main compliance issue is a possible residency or retention mismatch if regulated data is moved from the local project into Perplexity. The profiles do not show a specific regulated data class, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated or confidential data is uploaded to Perplexity
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the transferred documents
mitigations: Avoid uploading regulated data
Use anonymized excerpts only
Check vendor retention settings before use
Document the data flow in the project record
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA or approved residency configuration
